utterances.speaker: MS. IODICE
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. Good afternoon. Yesterday we were discussing the participation of Vojvoda Vasilije Vidovic, aka Vaske, in the battle-fields of Ilijas and Vogosca in the Greater Sarajevo area. Rajko Jankovic's VRS unit worked together with Vojvoda Vaske and his Seseljevci. During one of these joint operations in Crna Rijeka, Ilijas, Vaske killed a non-Serb civilian, as Witness Sejdic testified. The evidence also proves beyond a reasonable doubt that Vojvoda Vaske took part in the destruction of religious property after the take-over of Ilijas and Vogosca. VS-1055 testified that Vaske damaged or destroyed mosques and churches in Ilijas municipality during the course of 1992, including those in Ilijas, Ljesevo, Misoca, and Visoca. The accused claims that the Ilijas mosque was destroyed at the end of 1992, while Vaske was in Nisic. This claim is contradicted by the evidence on the record. Witness Dzafic, in Exhibit P840, describes how, in June 1992, he heard the explosion that destroyed the Stari Ilijas mosque and later heard Vaske's Seseljevci recounting how they had destroyed the mosque. Similarly, Exhibit P1045 confirms that the mosques in Misoca were destroyed in June 1992. With regards to Vogosca municipality, Witness Sejdic testified at transcript 8282 that Vaske destroyed the mosque in Svrake. The accused's attempts to confuse the witness were not persuasive and should be dismissed. Vojvoda Nikola Poplasen was also active in Vogosca, and throughout the second half of 1992 he was directly involved in the forced labour and exchange of non-Serbs as specified in Exhibit P975 and in paragraphs 408 through 410 of the Prosecution's closing brief. Despite the accused's claims to the contrary, the evidence proves beyond a reasonable doubt that Poplasen's link to the SRS and to the accused was firmly established already in early 1992. In the order promoting Poplasen to Vojvoda, which is Exhibit P218, the accused confirmed that Poplasen: "As of May 1992, he has been performing the duties of the president of the Serbian Radical Party for Republika Srpska." The accused confirmed this again in September 1992 in Exhibit P1205, stating that an SRS branch had already been established in Republika Srpska and Nikola Poplasen was its president. As the accused admitted, another one of his Vojvodas, Slavko Aleksic, was in Grbavica, Novo Sarajevo. In Exhibit P1102, Aleksic admitted arriving at the Jewish cemetery on the 21st of April, 1992, and together with his Seseljevci they were "clearing Grbavica." He soon controlled the area of what he defined as Serbian Grbavica, which he explained was one of the most difficult sections of the Serb defence lines, fiercely attacked by the Army of BiH because: "They knew that, if they broke through the lines of the defence at the Jewish cemetery, Grbavica would also fall, and Lukavica and everything else." Soon he gathered around him about 100 Seseljevci, volunteers from Serbia, but also from other countries, as shown in Exhibit P256, summarising the role of Aleksic and his link to the accused.

To me he's a Chetnik, you know. People might say he's communist or whatever, but he's kind of defended us too from the start. "Maggie O'Kane: Thank you very much."

utterances.speaker: MS. IODICE
utterances.text: It was Aleksic's Seseljevci who, together with other Serb forces, took over Grbavica and subjected its non-Serb population to a campaign of killings, arbitrary searches, and plunder, which forced them out of their homes, as detailed in paragraphs 384 through 387 of the Prosecution's closing brief. Another of the accused's Vojvoda, Branislav Gavrilovic, aka Brne, was active in Ilidza municipality. There, the Seseljevci co-operated with the Serb Crisis Staff of Nedjeljko Prstojevic to forcibly expel non-Serbs from the municipality. As the accused admitted at transcript 1935, Brne was transferred to Sarajevo from Slavonia by JNA helicopter. As Brne confirmed in Exhibit P999, this helicopter transfer was arranged thanks to his Vojvoda, Vojislav Seselj. The accused has heavily disputed the evidence of Witness Perica Koblar, who describes the joint VRS and Brne's Seseljevci action to capture Gola Brda on Mount Igman and the capture and murder of prisoners of war. The accused ignored that the same events have been described by Brne himself and by the accused's own periodical, "Velika Srbija," these are, in that order, Exhibit P999 and Exhibit P1000. The evidence shows beyond a reasonable doubt that on the 17th of July, 1993, four members of the Army of BiH, including Koblar, were captured by a group of Seseljevci under the command of Brne during an action which "Velika Srbija" describes as one of the typical successes of Vojvoda Brne and his Chetniks. As described in paragraphs 395 through 400 of the Prosecution's closing brief, Koblar was captured by a Seseljevac called Pajkovic, whose presence and role amongst Brne's Seseljevci is confirmed by Exhibit P1000. One of the prisoners of war, Robert Kahrimanovic, was murdered by a member of Brne's Seseljevci immediately upon capture. The remaining three were taken down Mount Igman to a clearing where Brne was waiting. Brne was introduced to the prisoners of war as "Chetnik Vojvoda, Branislav Gavrilovic," as described at transcript 8009. The prisoners of war were severely beaten and insulted with the ethnic slur "balija." Brne, upon learning that one of the prisoners of war, Zivko Krajisnik, was a Serb, kicked him, broke Krajisnik's nose with his fingers, and said: "Repeat that again. Say you're a Serb again and I'll rip your head off." Brne then ordered at transcript 8011: "Take him away. Take the trash away. Kill the trash." Krajisnik was taken a few metres away by one of Brne's Seseljevci and murdered. Another prisoner of war, Rusmir Hamalukic, was killed by Pajkovic. Koblar's evidence is credible, reliable, and coherent. There is no doubt that the Army of BiH soldiers were captured by Brne's Seseljevci. While the accused seems to dispute the insignia that Brne's Seseljevci had, he does not dispute that it was in fact Brne's Seseljevci, he admitted at transcript 8099: "... it was the Chetnik unit ... there is no dispute that they were called Chetniks and they called themselves Chetniks." The detail of the insignia is irrelevant. There is also no doubt that the Army of BiH soldiers were captured alive and then murdered by Brne and his Seseljevci. They were not killed in battle, as the accused claims. The detail of the capture was also recorded by "Velika Srbija," and Brne even bragged about it. He said in Exhibit P999: "We caught four Muslim fighters on the spot." The minor inconsistencies within Koblar's first statement, if any, have been clarified by him during his testimony. He stated how his statement to the BiH military authorities was given only two days after he had fled from detention. He never had the opportunity of reading it and was taken under time pressure. In conclusion, the evidence proves beyond a reasonable doubt that the crimes charged in relation to Greater Sarajevo were committed by members of the Serb forces, including Seseljevci. These crimes were an integral part of the common plan to ethnically cleanse Serb-targeted territories in BiH of its non-Serb population and create Serb-controlled areas. I will now give the floor to Mr. Traldi, who will describe how the same pattern of crimes repeated in Mostar and Nevesinje.

And now it turns out that five is really not enough. I'm not only the most renowned professor of law, but I also make very good estimates, almost as a clairvoyant.
